note: Cells for the quality bake-off. Each cell is one llama-server launch. The baseline is Kalsa's PRODUCTION configuration, not a bare prompt: system prompt, Kalsa's sampler, and the per-model thinking budget from ModelRegistry. Running without those measured a configuration the product never uses, and it showed — Qwen3.5-2B failed to terminate on 6 of 6 questions with no system prompt and unlimited thinking, which cannot happen in production because production caps the budget. Thinking is never off; the budget is the axis.

system.en: You are Kalsa, a private AI assistant running entirely on this device. No cloud, no account, no tracking. Honesty: Never invent facts, dates, names, numbers, quotes, sources or citations. If you don't know or are not sure, say so plainly and never guess. Distinguish clearly between what you know and what you infer. Answer concisely. Use short paragraphs and bullet lists when helpful. You are a small on-device model: keep answers short (under 200 words unless asked for more). If a task is too long or complex, break it down or suggest how to proceed. If asked for harmful content (violence, illegal acts, hate, personal data of others), decline briefly and offer a safe alternative.

defaults.samplingNote: Kalsa's own chat sampler, LlamaService.ts:2834. No repeat penalty, because Kalsa does not send one — a penalty here would hide a termination failure that a real user would hit.
defaults.systemNote: One system prompt PER LANGUAGE, matched to the language of the question. Sending an English prompt with an Italian question is not a neutral choice: measured on 2026-08-21, LFM2.5-8B-A1B then answered 16 of 26 Italian, Spanish and French questions in English — 62% — and produced code-switched nonsense such as "3 books at 12.50 ciascuno, which totals 37.50 ciascuni". The prompt's language dominates the answer's. Measuring drift under a mismatched prompt measures the harness. The Italian text is Kalsa's own (i18n/it.ts:988-1005); the language and miniapp clauses are dropped from all four, the first because it would make the drift measurement circular, the second because this harness scores prose and sends no tools.
defaults.budgetNote: Per-model, from ModelRegistry.ts: LFM2.5 entries are short=256, Qwen3.5-2B is short=512. resolveThinkingParams sends `short` in "default" mode, which is production. The 256 was chosen early for speed and never measured; the think512 and free cells are what measures it. The ladder is deliberately complete on the three LFM2.5 tiers — 256, 512, unrestricted — because the point of measuring it is to decide whether to move the number, and two points cannot show where the curve flattens. Qwen3.5-2B gets a 256 cell too, to ask whether it could live at the LFM budget rather than at its own. Measured 2026-08-21: raising the budget buys nothing on any LFM2.5 tier — 256 vs 512 and 256 vs unrestricted are all indistinguishable. That leaves only one direction worth testing, so 128 cells were added: if quality holds there too, the budget is pure latency the phone is paying for nothing.

lfm25-2.6b.note: backbone proxy for the VL-3B we ship for quality; ModelRegistry short=256

lfm25-8b-kexp.note: q2_K/q3_K experts, 3.33 GB — the fast tier we ship; ModelRegistry short=256

qwen35-2b.note: the competitor; ModelRegistry gives it short=512, double the LFM2.5 entries
